This relationship is supported by two distinct pathways: one involving 9-[(3R,4S,5R)-3,4-dihydroxy-5-(hydroxymethyl)oxolan-2-yl]-3H-purin-2-one, which is a known target of 1-Methoxyadamantane, and another involving 2,3,6-Trimethylbenzaldehyde, which also targets Neuropilin-2. Both pathways ultimately lead to the same target, Neuropilin-2, indicating a possible mechanism of action through HaCaT cells. The scores for these paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in the relationship, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The presence of multiple targets and their shared downstream effect on Neuropilin-2 supports a mechanistic link, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the specific role of 1-Methoxyadamantane in this process.
